source: Toy defense is a game where players use blocks to make bases and defend it with traps toy soldiers the game is wave based and every wave is locked until players beat the one before it players start with a basic toy soldier called a nebie and 5 paper blocks newbie is the weakest soldier and does 1 damadge every 2 seconds the paper blocks are to use to make a simple base and defend the soldiers. in wave the enemies are tan toy soldiers with no wepons they can only punch dealing 1 damdge every 2 seconds just like the newbie as player complete more waves the enemies become more stronger,more health gain wepons like knifs showels macheties guns they also look more advanced with more improvd armor and equipment players can save up money to buy crates which gives them new soldiers stronger blocks and traps and useful awards the game includes an invintory where players can store and equip their soldiers blocks and traps before battling the enemies the player can place it down the game should have high quality toy style models fun animations and coloufull maps whihc makes it feel like a toy bettlefield. More soldiers enemies waves bosses and features can be added as the game grows

answers.ask: Do enemies follow one fixed path to the base, or walk in from any edge across open ground?
answers.answer: Enemies walk in across open ground toward the player-built base, so players can design defenses around different approach angles.

answers.ask: How big is one battlefield, and is it one map per wave or one map reused?
answers.answer: Use one small battlefield map reused across waves, with enough open space for a simple base and enemy approaches.

answers.ask: Is this single player or several players sharing one base?
answers.answer: Make it single player for the first version, with the player building and defending their own base.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] shape — Q: Do enemies follow one fixed path to the base, or walk in from any edge across open ground? A: Enemies walk in across open ground toward the player-built base, so players can design defenses around different approach angles.
- [author] scale — Q: How big is one battlefield, and is it one map per wave or one map reused? A: Use one small battlefield map reused across waves, with enough open space for a simple base and enemy approaches.
- [author] goal — Q: Is this single player or several players sharing one base? A: Make it single player for the first version, with the player building and defending their own base.
- [agent_inferred] approach count — Q: How many distinct approach directions should the open battlefield support? A: Use four perimeter approach directions around the central base ground.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one small colorful toy battlefield reused across waves. Keep the ground broadly open, with a central player base area large enough for a simple fort made from toy blocks, traps, and toy-soldier placements. Arrange clear approach ground from four perimeter directions so tan enemy toy soldiers can advance dynamically rather than following a fixed lane. Use high-quality playful toy-style models, bright colors, and a readable tabletop-like composition while leaving most of the central land unobstructed for player construction. Mark a visible toy command piece at the heart of the base as the object being defended.

## Genre
The genre is Strategy.

## Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open`, Open Contested Terrain, because enemies path dynamically across open ground from several angles. The matching preset is Base Defense, retaining its defended core and wave origins while omitting prebuilt cover and destructible terrain that would obstruct player construction.

## Config requirements
Use `buildzone-plot` for broad open buildable land radiating around the player's base; and the image half of `tracker-core` for a colorful toy command piece anchoring the structure being defended. The toy block, trap, soldier, and enemy visual language is scene-specific; player-owned pieces are placed during play rather than prebuilt into the map.

## Layout requirements
Place the layout half of `tracker-core` at the exact centre of the buildable base ground. Place `spawner-npc` as exactly 4 enemy wave origins around the battlefield perimeter, one per approach direction, all facing the core across navigable open ground. Add one free-text `SpawnZone` with no canonical option ID beside the central base for the single player, protected from an immediate wave origin. The starting Newbie soldier and 5 paper blocks remain inventory items, not fixed map placements.

## Layout components
The build contains one reused battlefield, one central buildable base area, one defended toy core, one single-player start, four perimeter enemy origins, four open approach sectors, and a clear outer boundary. Avoid a fixed enemy lane, permanent towers, or prebuilt trap placements. The central area must support player-built block walls without sealing every approach.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the colorful toy-battlefield composition first and derive the top-down, because dynamic pathing across simple open terrain does not require a procedural lane.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium, preserving individual toy blocks while allowing four clear approach angles around a simple base. The theme is a bright, high-quality toy battlefield. The pipeline remains `P0`, since the map is one flat open surface reused across all waves.
